messages.subject: weak measurement invariance
parts:
hi,

"weak invariance" in a multi-group sem means that loadings are constrained to be equal across groups, right? in most papers i have seen people in general use the standardized loadings and i thought these are meant to be equal. however, when i fit a multiple group model in lavaan (without initial standardization of variables), the unstandarized loadings are equal, but standardized aren't; i suppose because the factors variance is not constrained to be equal (and when i add this constraint, the standardized loadings are equal between groups).

So, does it matter whether to initially standardize the ov or to constrain the lv-variance, when assessing weak invariance? or should one constrain only the loadings and report different standardized loadings? Any insight would be much appreciated!

and, one more question: what does this output from a summary of a multiple group model mean?

Scales y*:
    item_1             1.001    0.065   15.421    0.000
    item_2             1.058    0.068   15.593    0.000
    item_3             1.210    0.086   14.055    0.000
...


thanks a lot, hans

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: weak measurement invariance
parts:
On 12/09/2013 10:32 PM, Dr. Hans Hansen wrote:
> hi,
>
> "weak invariance" in a multi-group sem means that loadings are
> constrained to be equal across groups, right? in most papers i have seen
> people in general use the standardized loadings and i thought these are
> meant to be equal.

No. They may report standardized loadings, but in the analysis, you need
to use unstandardized loadings (otherwise you add another implicit
constraint: all observed variances are equal in all groups).
> constrain only the loadings and report different standardized loadings?

> and, one more question: what does this output from a summary of a
> multiple group model mean?
>
> Scales y*:
> item_1 1.001 0.065 15.421 0.000
> item_2 1.058 0.068 15.593 0.000
> item_3 1.210 0.086 14.055 0.000

These are the 'delta' scaling factors. They are used in a multiple group
analysis with categorical variables. See the following paper for more
information:

Muth�n, B. & Christoffersson, A. (1981). Simultaneous factor analysis of
dichotomous variables in several groups. Psychometrika, 46, 407-419.

Yves.
